content: 1. The purpose of this type of framework is to elucidate the causal relationships that link the step-by-step achievement of results to the impact of interventions. 2. A Software Requirements Specification (SRS) is a document that details the technical requirements of a desired system. It clearly outlines the expectations and needs from the team of health experts and project managers for the developers tasked with creating the project’s digital health system. 3. Stability refers to the probability that a technical system’s functions will not change or fail during use. In this context, stability specifically denotes the ability of a digital health system to remain operational under both normal and anticipated peak data load conditions. 4. Stakeholders are individuals or organizations with a vested interest in the digital health system or intervention. They may act as decision-makers, project staff, or end-users. 5. Summative evaluation is a study conducted at the conclusion of an intervention, or a specific phase of it, to assess the extent to which the anticipated outcomes were achieved. 6. A theory of change is a causal model that connects outcomes and activities, providing an explanation of how and why the desired change is expected to occur. 7. Theory-based conceptual frameworks, while similar to logic models, aim to offer a deeper understanding of the complex relationships between program activities and the anticipated results. 8. Usability is defined as the extent to which a product or system can be used by specified users to achieve specific goals effectively, efficiently, and satisfactorily within a defined context of use. 9. Use cases are narrative descriptions that illustrate how a target user performs a specific task using the technology, as well as how the system is expected to respond in each scenario. 10. A value proposition is a statement that outlines the benefits provided to end-users, often with an implicit comparison to a non-digital intervention or an alternative digital product. 11. Wireframes are simple, schematic illustrations that depict the content, layout, functions, and behavior of the target system. They are useful for visualizing the expected functionality of a system.
